en: ...Captain.
Yes, thank you. I'm okay. I've\ncalmed down.
Are you feeling alright?
The equipment here couldn't\nhandle my body, so I performed\na self-repair.
That's a bit blunt, but I'm just\nglad you're feeling better.
Whether I'm "better"... I don't\nknow.
...Captain, did you hear?

My father and Edge Maverick
were supposed to have purged
the Phantom from this
universe.
Asmodeus, the\nCommander-in-Chief of the\nOber Space Force.

Good grief. I thought I was
done with the likes of
negotiating directly with the
leader of one side in the middle
of a war.

...Based on what I've heard,
may I assume that you are all
agreeing to side with the Raza
Space Force?

Now, now, that's not exactly it.
We're simply going to meet this
Asmodeus. I never said
anything about defeating him.

He is not the kind of person
you can just meet simply by
deciding to go see him. No
matter how you look at it, it will
lead to combat.
In the end, you would be\ncontributing to the victory of\nthe Raza army.

We aren't intervening in the
war between Raza and Ober.
We are merely going to
investigate a crisis that could
potentially threaten the entire
universe.

I admit that's a bit of a
sophistry. If we encounter
Asmodeus, combat will be
inevitable, and if you call that
intervening, then it is.

If Raza ends up winning as a
result, the people of Ober will
likely point fingers at us. Even
so...

This is no longer mere
intervention in the Azurite
system. This is a fight to
protect the safety of the
entire universe.
I don't know if they are\nsurvivors or if they've been\nnewly born.

Of course, we won't ask for
any more help from Jeanne or
Isabel's group. That would
make the level of intervention
too great.
So, from here on, we'll use our\nown ship...
Wait!
Oh, Euwin? What's wrong?
Captain, everyone... uh...\nLavarnia has something to say.
Huh?
I will be the one to transport\nyou all aboard the Overman!
But... as a Hardier Warrior of\nMorphus, I cannot let them run\nwild.

Captain. This isn't just an
interstellar war. It's a crisis
that threatens every living soul
in the universe.
I cannot run away from this\nfight. Please...
Yes, I understand. We only\ncame here to confirm your\nintentions, Valka.
What?
As people born on Earth and\nas members of the Galactic\nFederation's military,
we can no longer simply ignore\nthe conflict between Raza and\nOber.
Did... something happen?
It may not be as simple as\nending the war, like it was with\nDaftine.

But even if we find Eve and
bring her back now, we cannot
simply leave the Azurite
system.
...And what does everyone else\nthink?

Our individual goals may differ,
but we are all in agreement
that we cannot stand by and
watch the battle between Raza
and Ober.
I see. That's a relief. I thought\nRicardo might be against it.
We thought so too. But Ricardo\nwas actually the first one to\nagree.
What?

He seems to suspect a
connection to whoever shot
down the starship Ricardo and
Tika were on 200 years in the
future.

The Azurite system 200 years
from now should be peaceful
according to what Ricardo
knows, so I don't think there's
a direct connection, but...
No, that's fine. With this many\ncomrades, it's only natural that\nwe all think differently.

As long as we're all united in
the belief that we can't just
stand by and watch Raza and
Ober fight, that's all that
matters.
You're absolutely right.

What do you think, Valka?
We're about to have a meeting
with Heath, Lavarnia, and
Kevin...
...to decide on our next course\nof action.
Yeah, I'm ready. I can go now...

I have to conduct myself in a
way that brings no shame to
the Hardier Warrior of
Morphus.
That's the spirit!
The <font color=yellow>Missing Procedure</font>, is it?

Yeah. An "unknown will" that
warps the laws of the universe
and changes the very nature
of existence.
Our guides in Morphus, the\n"Ex," referred to it as the\nMissing Procedure.

That Phantom fleet analyzed
the energy information of living
organisms naturally existing
throughout this universe,
and replaced them with\nimmutable existences.

Turning living things into
immutable existences... now
we're talking some seriously big
concepts. You're saying Ober is
doing something with a thing
that makes no sense?

<font color=blue>Valka</font>: If it possesses the same
properties as the Missing
Procedure my father once
faced, there is a high
probability that someone in
Ober is being manipulated.

<font color=blue>Kevin</font>: Since you can analyze it
to that extent, has a
countermeasure for this
situation been established?

<font color=blue>Valka</font>: Of course. The
Phantoms have a source. I
propose that we track down
and annihilate that source.
<font color=blue>Verda</font>: A source, eh? So you're\nsaying they have something\nlike a nest.

<font color=blue>Valka</font>: That is a correct
understanding. Specifically, a
substance called "Grigori"
absorbs surrounding
information to create
Phantoms.
<font color=blue>Verda</font>: Grigori?
<font color=blue>Valka</font>: Just imagine a\ncrystal-like stone that glows\npurple.

They vary in size, but based on
what Captain Jeanne said, if
we assume it's the same as
the previous battle, it should
be quite large.
<font color=blue>Ricardo</font> So, if we smash that\nGrigori, does that mean the\nPhantoms will vanish?
<font color=blue>Valka</font> Exactly. However, I have\none question.

We, the Hardier Warrior of
Morphus―meaning EnII―fought
the Grigori over 500 years ago.
Naturally, research has
progressed since then.

Given that, I find it hard to
believe that Ex would have
overlooked a Grigori of that
size remaining here.
<font color=blue>Mastima</font> Good grief, here he\ngoes again with his Ex-worship.
<font color=blue>Tika</font> Mastima!

<font color=blue>Valka</font> ...Looking back at the
history of Morphus, the scale
of the disaster caused by
Master Mastima's Moonshadow
Ladder is on a completely
different level than a Grigori.

If this really were the work of a
Grigori, I would have been
dispatched to the Azurite
system myself. Because the
threat level is just so different!

<font color=blue>Mastima</font> What?! Are you saying
those ghosts are a greater
threat than the Moonshadow
Ladder I created?! Take it
back! Especially for someone
who's just a lackey of
Vandione!
<font color=blue>Verda</font> This is hardly the time\nor place for a competition...
<font color=blue>Tika</font> Mastima! Just be quiet\nalready! We're not getting\nanywhere!
<font color=blue>Mastima</font> Shut up, Tika! How\ncan I stay quiet after being\ntold something like thaaaaat...!
<font color=blue>Tika</font> Honestly! Valka, please\ncontinue!

<font color=blue>Valka</font> Hehe. Anyway, there are
too many unnatural points
regarding this Phantom
incident.

But if you think back, we
encountered something similar
to the Phantoms even before
we entered the Azurite system.
<font color=blue>Tika</font> ...The black monsters Givel\nsummoned. ...And... Eve's...
<font color=blue>Mastima</font> Hmph! Hmph!!
<font color=blue>Tika</font> Ma-sti-ma! Be quiet!!
<font color=blue>Henri</font> Are you suggesting that\nGivel is the one creating the\nPhantoms now?
<font color=blue>Valka</font> That's what I'd like to\nsay... but there are still\nquestions.
Givel's goal in Daftine was to\ncross the boundary between\nadjacent universes.
That's why the Thornite, which\nstabilizes space, should have\nbeen a vital element for him.
Yet, in Lazuli, the Phantoms\nand the Thornite were in\nconflict.
<font color=blue>Tika</font> Now that you mention it,\nthat's true.

<font color=blue>Heath</font> Those guys showed
some real guts facing off
against the black McKinley
ships.

<font color=blue>Valka</font> Furthermore, Phantoms
are fundamentally hostile to all
life. That makes it all the more
inexplicable that they are
currently acting only in Ober's
favor.
The problem lies in the footage\nof Lady Leash that Lady Carlin\nsummoned at the Urza System.
<font color=blue>Karlyn</font> You mean the one\nwhere Eve saw Givel?

<font color=blue>Valka</font> If that was a recording
from after we defeated Givel...
then I suspect the person
appearing alongside Givel holds
the key to this situation.

<font color=blue>Karlyn</font> You mean someone is
controlling Givel, just like Givel
was controlling the Beast
Witches?
To be able to do something like\nthat to Givel...
It is possible.
What?
There is one person who could\ndo it. At least, if my and the\nCaptain's theories are correct.

I heard from Jeanne. The
current Commander-in-Chief of
the Ober Space Force is
named Asmodeus.
If there is anyone capable of\nmanipulating Givel, it can be\nnone other than Asmodeus!

Asmodeus is the name of the
King of the Demon Realm,
known as the "Demon King" on
the planet Roak at the far
edge of the galaxy, who led an
army of monsters in an
attempt to annihilate the
humans of Roak.
The Demon Realm, huh?\nMastima mentioned something\nlike that before.
It is said... that Asmodeus was\na being who harbored a deep\nhatred for humanity.

He led the Ober humans―who
are called monsters in other
star systems―and remained
hostile to the people of planet
Roak for many years.

...In the footage we saw from
the Urza System, there was
someone else standing beside
Givel, right?
You're saying that figure was\nAsmodeus?
I believe that is highly likely.
Regardless, whether we are\nuncovering the secrets of the\nPhantom,
or searching for Eve and Givel,\nthe clue we should be pursuing\nis...
A few hours later...
Is the Overman all fixed up?
...Yeah. Isabel's technicians\nhandled all the major repairs.
It's frustrating, but the experts\nreally are amazing.
I see. That's good news.
...Euwin. Shouldn't you be at\nthe meeting?
I still don't understand the\ncomplicated space stuff.

I figured it was enough for me
to know that we might end up
fighting the ghosts of our
friends' pasts.
...You're taking this surprisingly\nwell.
I trust the Captain's judgment.

More importantly, I noticed
Welch disappeared from the
meeting, so I came looking for
her...

...She's fine. Welch is over
there, listening intently to one
of the Isabel people explain
how the Warp Drive works.
That's a relief. I was worried\nshe might be messing around\nwith Isabel's equipment.

She seemed to enjoy watching
the Overman being repaired.
There was nothing for you to
worry about, Euwin.
I'm glad... but still, I'm really\nsorry.
Huh?
For breaking the Overman\nbecause of our own\ncircumstances.
...It's okay. It's been fixed, so\nI'm not worried about it\nanymore.
Even so, you've spent years\nbuilding this ship piece by\npiece, haven't you, Lavarnia?
that you carefully crafted,\nchoosing every single part for\nthe Overman.
...It's not your fault, Euwin. I'm\nthe one who decided to take\neveryone out into space.
...Thank you.
...You're the first person to\never say something like that to\nme.
What?
In terms of specs, the Overman\nisn't actually that great of a\nship.
Is that so?
I think the software\nperformance improved since\nCoro is on board,

but even then, a ship built and
maintained by a family in a
Bazaar dock would probably be
far superior.

It doesn't even have a warp
drive like a warship. If it
weren't for Eve, the Overman
would never have been used
for a deal like this.
I see...
My father saw me tuning the\nOverman and tried to give me\nplenty of high-end parts.
But I refused. Because if I did...
...You really value the feelings\nof those who create things,\ndon't you, Euwin?
Welch has always been that\nway.
...Welch?

Welch's family are blacksmiths,
so she's been dragged into
making all sorts of tools since
she was young.
Dragged into, not "helped out\nwith," huh?
Exactly. She was basically a\nguinea pig for all kinds of\nexperiments.
Hehe, I see.
While making all those things,\nWelch always insisted on them\nbeing "originals."

Sometimes she'd say she had
to gather the materials herself
and would keep the shop
closed for ages.

She was determined that one
day she'd make a sword for me
that surpassed the blueprints
Coro gave her.

In the end, that's what led me,
someone from an undeveloped
planet, to venture out into
space.
Thanks to that, Welch... she\nfound friends who truly\nunderstand her.
...Eh? D-do you mean me?
Yeah. The captain and the\nothers have accepted Welch,\ntoo, but...

The Captain and the others
accept Welch, but you're the
first person, Lavarnia, to
actually share in the joy and
excitement of creating things
with her.

If we can manage to resolve
the Captain's troubles and
return to the Stardust Bazaar,
I'd be happy if you could
continue being friends with
Welch.
...Wait, what do you mean?

We managed to send Heath
back to the mothership, but
from here on, we'll likely be
heading straight into the
middle of the war between
Raza and Ober.
...No way.

Of course, we'll properly
compensate you later for the
ship Eve damaged and the
Gems that were stolen.
...That's... not necessary\nanymore.
Huh?

I received more than enough in
exchange for the Gems. It's
more than enough to cover the
damaged ship, too. So...
If you're willing, I want you to\nstay on the Overman with me\nfrom here on.
W-wait, Lavarnia. You don't\nmean you want to stay with\nus...

It's too dangerous! To be
honest, even I have no idea
what's going to happen from
here on out!

Eh, wait, are you okay, Mr.
Euwin?! Ms. Welch, you just hit
him in the head with a
wrench...!
I'm fine, I'm fine. Eu-bo isn't\ngonna die from something like\nthat.
Ugh...! I could die! If it hit the\nwrong spot, I could totally die!!
Which is exactly why you didn't\ndie, since it hit the right spot!
More importantly, Eu-bo! I don't\nrecall raising you to be such a\nheartless man!
I don't recall raising you my\nfoot! Stop being so reckless\nfor once!

You just confessed to Lover
that you "volunteered for the
beautiful Welch-chan's
experiments since you were a
kid."
I never said a single word of\nthat!!
Yeah, yeah, whatever. Anyway,\nLover says she wants to come\nalong.

So, if the Captain and the
others try to send Lover back
to the Bazaar after this, Eu-bo,
you're teaming up with me to
oppose them, got it?

What?! No, but... there's no
reason for Ms. Lavarnia to
throw herself into danger like
that...!

She wants to challenge the
world with something she
created. That's more than
enough of a reason!
What!?

Anyway, we're probably just
going to go blast those
black-clad creeps or go look
for Eve and Givel.

But you're not planning on
going around explaining all that
to the people of Raza and
Ober, right?
Well... probably not.

But if we keep wandering
around here in Coro's ship, the
people of Raza and Ober who
don't know the situation...
...might start keeping a close\neye on Daftine. That part\ndoesn't change, does it?
I... I guess not.

If we don't want to be seen as
favoring either Raza or Ober,
we can't just go around using
Isabel however we want.
So, which ship can we move\nfreely right now, and who owns\nit?
...Ms. Welch.

Right now, we're actually in a
position where we should be
bowing our heads and begging
Lover to come with us! Get a
grip, Euwin!
...I mean, yes, I suppose... but\nit's not like I don't understand\nthat...

Now that you get it, get
moving! Go stop the Captain
and the others before they
decide to call Rekoro!
I-I get it, I get it! Just stop\nswinging that wrench around!
...Um, Ms. Welch, why?
Because it looked like fun,\nobviously.
Huh?
Flying through space in your\nown ship was fun, wasn't it?

You built it yourself, after all,
so I totally get it. It's a great
feeling to see something you
made working exactly as it
should.
...Ms. Welch.

Do you mind sticking around a
bit longer? Our Captain, Coro,
Eu, Verda, Tika, Karlyn, Valka,
Henri, and Ricardo...

They all have this habit of
wanting to shoulder everything
themselves. They always try to
take on all the trouble, acting
all serious even when nobody
asked them to.

Being thoughtless is bad, but I
think it's about time they
realized that making the most
of what you have isn't a bad
thing.
In that regard, I really wish\nthey'd take a page out of\nMastima's book.
...Hey, Welch.
Hmm?
Right now, we have no choice\nbut to use the Overman, even\nif it's been modified for Raza...
But when this is all over... I\nwant to build a new ship from\nscratch. Would you help me?
Of course! I'd be happy to!

Come on, Lover, tell her. If you
don't give the okay, my
stubborn crew will just be
suspicious.
...Okay!
Are you being serious?
Yes, Boss!
...Are you sure?
...Y...Yes, Boss!!
I sense some hesitation.
Yes, Boss!!! I'm going with them!
Is that not a violation of the\nservice regulations?
You fired me, Boss! I'm not\neven a soldier anymore!!
I see. I will not allow it.
Why not?! This was supposed\nto be the part where you let\nme go!!

They are not evil people. I can
see that they possess superior
technology and that each of
them is a powerful warrior.

However, this is a war. Such
things are no guarantee of
safety. I have no intention of
sending my subordinates
blindly into a death trap.
Boss! But...!
That is also the promise I made\nto your parents.
...Therefore, I will absolutely not\nallow you to accompany them.
Boss... I...
Eek!? W-what is it?
Listen to me, Heath Bureau. I\nwill not allow it.
Huh?
I must keep my promise to\nyour parents. I will not allow\nyou to accompany them.

Isabel is no longer being
questioned for treason, so I will
no longer assign my
subordinates to excessively
dangerous missions.
...Boss...
Unlike back then, you are an\nadult now. I will not allow it.
...Yes, Boss!!
Now that you understand,\nreturn to your original post as\nordered.
Yes, Boss!! Thank you!!

I have done nothing worthy of
thanks. You know exactly how
those who defy my orders are
treated... don't you?
Yes, Boss! Excuse me!!

...Good grief. To make the
"Demon of Marswest" go to
such lengths... he really is slow.
I only hope he doesn't hold
them back.
The vigor of youth is quite\ndazzling to an old man.
I am still young myself.
Of course, I include you in that.\nAs far as I'm concerned, all\nRaza are like children.
If you are indeed the one and\nonly Kevin Barktain, then I\nsuppose that is true.
In all honesty, do you believe\nthey can achieve their goal?

It is the duty of the elderly to
believe in the youth. I have
spent far too long acting
superior to them; I shouldn't be
a burden now.
...I see.

Yes, we shall do what must be
done. We must at least pave
the way for the children to
follow.
...But are you certain? Your\nship's position will only worsen.

It's too late for that. It's not as
if my standing has recovered.
Being the one to fill the gaps in
such a desperate war is
practically the same as being
executed for treason.

...In that case, I shall share the
research results I accumulated
in Lazuli along the way. I am
sure you will find them most
intriguing.
All crew, check your harnesses.\nThe Overman is launching!

Systems are all green. No
space vessels or excessive
concentrations of silicon-based
matter detected in the vicinity.
I judge that we will be safe for
a while.

Alright, let's go over the plan.
Thanks to Isabel's group, we
know the state of the war, but
we've jumped out here without
any idea of the current
situation.

We don't even know where our
comrade Eve is, so how are we
supposed to track down Givel
and Asmodeus?
I have an idea about that.\nPlease, listen!
Hm?

I have been awaiting this
communication. I have just
finished constructing the
requested program.
Rekoro!
I have already completed the\ncreation of a full star map of\nthe Azurite system.

With this, we can narrow down
the location of the "Grigori"
mentioned by Valka S90, or
the command center of the
Phantom fleet.
What do you mean?

We will take advantage of the
fact that battles between Raza
and Ober are occurring
incessantly within the Azurite
system.

The method itself is simple.
Basically, we just observe the
combat status of the Raza
forces and the concentration
of silicon-based materials
across the entire system...

I see. If the Raza ships are
engaging in combat despite no
reaction from the Ober ships,
there is a high probability that
a Phantom is present.
Exactly. Coro has also\nprovided feedback on the\ncurrent specs of the Overman.

By considering the Phantom's
appearance location and the
ship's specs, we will lure them
toward the location most likely
to house the command tower.
Hmph. Your ship's\nperformance is as insane as\never.
Naturally. We modified it using\nthe full strength of Ex Giva...\nHm?
Yo. Why the weird face?
Heath!? Why are you here!?
Huh!? Heath wasn't included in\nthe weight calculations when\nwe left Isabel!
...I left the Gems container to\npay for the Overman's repairs.
What!?
We finally made it back to the\nmothership; what on earth\nwere you thinking?

What am I thinking? It's
obvious. I'm thinking about
protecting the peace of the
universe where I was born.
Heath...

During the meeting, you guys
were all fired up about some
grudge from a distant part of
space. But this is the Azurite
system, where I was born.

If you all are going to face a
cosmic crisis starting from the
Azurite system, how can I,
someone born here, just stand
by and do nothing?
Did you get permission from\nyour boss?
As if my boss would ever give\nme permission.
Hmph, I figured.
No way! Then wouldn't that be\na violation of orders...?

The moment I was kicked out
in a life pod, I stopped being a
soldier. Orders don't even
apply to me anymore.

Whether some superior officer
forgives a non-soldier or not
has absolutely nothing to do
with me.

Little Eu used to use that kind
of logic to talk back to her
family, too. Though she's
suddenly become so stiff
lately, probably because life's
been so peaceful.
Ugh... well, I mean...
There's no reason why Lover\ncan travel with you guys but I\ncan't.

Then there's the matter of
Lover's old man. If Lover gets
seriously hurt, that old geezer
won't stop until he's wiped out
both Raza and Ober.
Protecting Lover is basically\nthe same as protecting the\npeace of the Azurite system.

...I'm not so weak that I need
Heath to protect me, and he's
just saying whatever he wants,
but I figured he'd be even more
reckless if I refused, so I'm
reluctantly agreeing.

...Since Ms. Lavarnia is the
owner of this ship, I'll go along
with it for now, but please let
me know next time because
the weight calculations scare
me...
...Understood.

Anyway, if we use Rekoro's
analysis to take down the
Phantoms one by one, we'll
eventually hit the Phantoms'
nest.

And if your enemy Givel or that
problematic
Commander-in-Chief Asmodeus
are involved with the
Phantoms,

they might eventually lose
patience and show their hand.
All we have to do is pounce on
that!
Precisely.
See? Simple and clear. ...Hey,\nCaptain.

I said what I said earlier, but
I'm a Razan, I've got plenty of
Ober friends, and I owe my life
to that old geezer at the
Stardust Bazaar.

I'm not thinking of anything as
grandiose as stopping the war,
but if there's something behind
it all eating away at the Azurite
system, I want to stand up to
it.
Let me join you.
Yeah! Heath, glad to have you\nwith us!
Crew registration... well, we're\non the Overman now, so that\nshould be fine.
Have you reached an\nagreement? Very well, I shall\ntransmit the initial analysis.

Fortunately, there is a point
near the Overman where a
Phantom is expected to
appear. Proceed there
immediately.
All right! Let's move!

Stop taking charge. I'm the
captain now. Change course
for the predicted Phantom
appearance point, full speed
ahead!
Roger!!

After analyzing AI Rekoro's
data, we've narrowed down the
location significantly. There are
eight points where the
appearance frequency is high.

That's surprisingly few. I
thought they'd be appearing in
massive swarms all over the
place.

The sensors on the Raza
army's warships might find it
difficult to detect silicon, which
is a common substance in
space.
Furthermore, their black\nexterior makes them hard to\nspot visually.

Still, it doesn't seem like the
Raza side is just sitting idly by.
Looking at the battles over the
last few days, the Raza fleet
doesn't seem to have suffered
any major losses.

Exactly. That's why I consulted
with the Captain, Administrator
Koro, Mista Heath, and Lady
Lavarnia...

...and from those eight points,
we've narrowed the location of
the command tower down to
three.
Near Lazuli, the "Space Base\nCluster," and the "Asteroid\nBelt." Why these three?

The area near Lazuli is where
the biggest fireworks go off.
There are plenty of Ober ships
stationed there, so if
someone's controlling
Phantoms, there's a lot to
blend in with.
...The second location is an\narea with many of Ober's\nmilitary space bases.

However, compared to other
locations, they've been
repelling Raza ships with a high
success rate relative to their
defensive strength.
As for the last one, it's a small\nmining asteroid belt.

It's a place that should have
been abandoned due to low
mineral deposits, yet every now
and then, Raza ships are
reported as casualties.
Now that we've narrowed down\nthe locations, shall we begin\nthe operation immediately?

Yes. I don't know if Asmodeus
or Givel are there, or if Grigori
exists as Valka mentioned,
but...

The longer we wait, the more
Raza casualties will mount. We
should strike the points we've
